sources.entry: Context Engineering Kit by Vlad Goncharov - Hand-crafted collection of advanced context engineering techniques and patterns with minimal token footprint focused on improving agent result quality.

summary.one_liner: A marketplace of Claude Code plugins (also usable with other agents) that bundles prompts, sub-agents, and rules for improving agent output quality through reflection, judging, specification-driven development, and code review.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a plugin marketplace for AI coding agents, installed per plugin in Claude Code via /plugin install. Plugins cover reflection and memory curation (/reflect, /memorize, /critique), subagent-driven task execution with judge verification (/do-and-judge, /do-in-steps, /judge), and a spec-driven workflow (/add-task, /plan-task, /implement-task) built on the arc42 documentation standard. Other plugins provide multi-agent code and PR review, Git commit and PR commands, TDD commands, FPF structured hypothesis reasoning, Kaizen root-cause analysis, Domain-Driven Design and Clean Architecture rules, TypeScript rules, and MCP server setup guides. The README also includes a comparison table estimating accuracy and token overhead for different workflows, though those figures are the authors' own reported numbers. Gemini CLI and Antigravity CLI install all plugins as one bundle, and Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode get skills only through npx skills.
use_cases: Improve quality of code an AI agent writes
Review local changes or pull requests with multiple agents
Break a large coding task into specified steps with quality gates
Analyze root causes of bugs using Five Whys or fishbone methods
Set up MCP servers such as Context7 or Serena for a project
Enforce Clean Architecture, SOLID, or DDD rules during code writing
stack: GitHub CLI (used by Git plugin commands)
notable: Per-plugin install in Claude Code so only chosen agents and skills load into context
Spec-driven workflow based on the arc42 architecture documentation standard
Reliability table comparing one-shot, reflect, judge, and planned workflows by number of changed files
Multi-agent review plugin with impact and confidence filtering and a GitHub Actions option
Cross-agent support for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Cursor, Codex, and OpenCode, with reduced features outside Claude Code
caveats: Gemini CLI and Antigravity CLI cannot install individual plugins; all are installed as one bundle
Non-Claude-Code installs via npx skills do not include subagents
The FPF plugin loads a roughly 600k-token specification into a subagent and can consume token limits quickly
The spec-driven workflow can take from 30 minutes to a few days and is most useful for complex or existing codebases
